_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution: the mutation vocabulary belongs to ONE subset of ONE standard of ONE artifact, so its oracle registration and catalog live here rather than in a shared manifest. `stdio.semio.value` is a semio-NATIVE format — no third party reads or writes `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` for it — so the reference registered below is a second IMPLEMENTATION in another language rather than a third-party package.

oracles.rationale:
No library in any ecosystem reads or writes semio's own `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope, so the second producer a differential comparison needs is a second IMPLEMENTATION. `../../../../../../🧪️tests/mutate-semio-value/🐍️component.py` is that implementation: the semio envelope, the recursive `[hex(schema),<value>,[<node>,…]]` DSL grammar, the tag-prefixed `SemioValue` production and all nine verbs with their inverses — including the ORDER-restoring multi-step undo `remove-map-entry` needs, because `set-map-entry` appends an absent key — written in Python from the committed specification documents alone: `../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/📝️text/📖️.grammar.semio`, `../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/💾️binary/📡️.protocol.semio`, `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/🔣️.json` and the committed `(before, mutation, after)` vectors. It imports nothing from and transliterates nothing of the Rust it judges, and it needs no host package, which is why `package` is empty. The `semio-value-mutation-semantics` no-oracle decision this entry replaces had named `json` 0.12 (json-rust) as the nearest candidate and declined it on evidence: a generic JSON DOM has no analogue for `Bytes`, `Ref`, lexeme-preserving `Int`/`Float` or the top-level id-keyed node graph, so every one of the nine semantics would still have been hand-written on top of it. That judgement stands. Python's `json` module IS used, for the job it is authoritative about — reading the real committed 424 KB `spatial.modelspace` building model once, with `parse_int`/`parse_float` hooks so every numeric source lexeme survives, to derive the document the case mutates — and `payload-fidelity` re-reads that same source on the subject side with this repository's own `stdio.json` RFC 8259 codec, so the two parsers are compared against each other as well.

UNDER PROTOCOL V2 this registration is classified `cross-semio-implementation` — a required SUPPLEMENTAL oracle that does not discharge `semio-v1-value-mutate`'s external-oracle requirement for its 9-kind mutation vocabulary; a qualifying third-party reference (`third-party-library` / `third-party-cli` / `standards-reference-tool`) is still owed.
